title: Astrolabe
intro: This is an astrolabe, a hand-held model of the sky. It was used to tell the time and to find where stars and the sun are.
provenance: Exact workshop and findspot not recorded in this catalogue entry.
facts: The rete is the cut-away star map on top. It turns over the fixed plate beneath to show the sky at different hours.
The rule is a pivoting arm used with the degree scale on the rim to read a star's height above the horizon.
Astrolabes were used for timekeeping, navigation on land, surveying and finding the direction of prayer.
Brass was the usual material because it can be engraved finely and does not rust.
unknown: The maker and original owner of this astrolabe are not recorded, and the exact date is an estimate.
